items.pronunciation_notes: Two long syllables with a clean break: aa jaa-naa.

learn.explanation_en: जाना as a vector marks completion, and with verbs of motion or change it marks that the change has actually happened. वह आ गया is "he's arrived" — more definite than वह आया, which just says he came. Both आना and जाना are intransitive, so there is no ने anywhere and the verb agrees with the subject: वह आ गई for a woman. The imperative आ जाओ is everywhere in spoken Hindi and is warmer than plain आओ — closer to "come on over" than to "come".

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both correct. गया says the arrival is complete and he is here; आया reports that he came.

examples.note: Both verbs intransitive, so no ने.
Warmer than plain आओ; very common in speech.
The vector agrees with the subject, because there is no ने to change that.

common_error.why_en: Neither आना nor जाना is transitive, so ने has nothing to attach to.

practice.prompt_en: He has arrived and is here now. Pick the vector.
practice.question: वह आ ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: जाना marks the completed arrival, and it brings no ने with it.

game.question_en: You want to say he's arrived — he is here now.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct Hindi. आ गया says the arrival is complete; आया reports it; the last two describe it in progress or as a habit.

items.gloss_en: to become, to get done — a change of state

learn.explanation_en: हो जाना is the workhorse of change. काम हो गया, the work is done. वह बीमार हो गया, he fell ill — not "was ill" but "became ill". देर हो गई, it's got late, with देर feminine so the vector is गई. The plain हुआ exists and reports that something happened; हो गया adds that a state has been crossed into. If you learn one जाना compound, learn this one. It is everywhere, and it is the natural way to say that something is now done.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both correct. हो गया says the work is now in a finished state; हुआ says it happened.

examples.note: A state has been reached.
Became ill, rather than was ill.
देर is feminine, so गई.

common_error.why_en: होना and जाना are both intransitive, so no ने.

practice.prompt_en: The subject is देर, which is feminine. Complete the compound.
practice.question: देर हो ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: देर is feminine singular, and with no ने the verb agrees with it.

game.question_en: You want to say the work is finished — the state has changed.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. हो गया marks the crossing into a finished state; the others report, generalise, or describe it in progress.

items.gloss_en: to fall asleep — the moment of crossing

learn.explanation_en: सोना is to sleep; सो जाना is to fall asleep — the moment of crossing rather than the state itself. वह सो गया. Compare वह सोया, closer to "he slept", and वह सो रहा है, "he is sleeping". Hindi keeps these three apart cleanly where English leans on context. Notice the pattern forming across this level: जाना turns up wherever a boundary is crossed — arriving, becoming, falling asleep. That is the single idea behind all three items.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both correct. सो गया is the moment of falling asleep; सोया is closer to "he slept".

examples.note: The moment of crossing over.
Still no ने; सोना is intransitive.
The state, not the crossing. No vector needed at all.

common_error.why_en: सोना is intransitive, and so is जाना.

practice.prompt_en: The child has fallen asleep. Pick the vector.
practice.question: बच्चा सो ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: जाना marks the crossing into sleep.

game.question_en: You want to say he fell asleep — the moment it happened.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. सो गया is the crossing; the others are the event, the state, and the habit.

summary.recap_en: जाना marks a boundary crossed — arriving, becoming, falling asleep. It is intransitive, so जाना compounds never take ने and the verb agrees with the subject. हो जाना is the one to learn first; it is everywhere.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the जाना compound that refuses ने even though its main verb is transitive.

levels.title_hi: खा गया · भूल गया · चला गया

items.gloss_en: to eat the lot — and the compound that takes no ने

learn.title_en: A transitive verb whose compound takes no ने
learn.explanation_en: This is the most surprising fact in the module. खाना is transitive. Module 9 spent sixteen levels teaching you that a perfective transitive takes ने. And वह सब खा गया takes none. The rule governing compounds is stricter than the one for simple verbs: ने appears only when the main verb and the vector are both transitive. खाना is transitive but जाना is not, so the compound behaves intransitively — the subject stays plain and the verb agrees with the subject, giving वह खा गई for a woman. The nuance of खा जाना is "ate the lot, polished it off", usually with a hint that it was more than expected.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both correct — and notice the subject changes shape between them. The plain transitive takes ने; the जाना compound does not.

examples.note: No ने, because जाना is intransitive.
लेना is transitive, so ने returns. Same main verb, opposite marking.

examples.english: She polished off all the sweets.
examples.note: The verb agrees with the subject, not with मिठाई.

common_error.why_en: The compound is intransitive because जाना is, so there is nothing for ने to attach to.

practice.prompt_en: He polished off the lot. Pick the vector.
practice.question: वह सब खा ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: गया — and notice the subject is वह, not उसने. With लिया the sentence would have to be उसने सब खा लिया.

game.question_en: He polished off the lot — more than you would have expected.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct Hindi. खा गया carries the sense of polishing it off; खा लिया just finishes it; the first reports it and the last is habitual. Note the subject marking changes with the vector.

items.gloss_en: to clean forget — the everyday form

learn.title_en: The verb that already refused ने
learn.explanation_en: भूलना was one of Module 9's three exceptions — it takes no ने on its own. Add जाना and it takes none for a second reason as well. वह नाम भूल गया is the ordinary everyday way to say you forgot something; the bare वह नाम भूला is correct but sounds bookish beside it. Two independent rules pointing the same way is worth noticing, because it means you cannot get this one wrong by reasoning from either direction.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both correct and both without ने. The compound is what people actually say; the bare form reads as literary.

examples.note: The everyday form.
No object at all, and still no ने.
किताब is feminine and the verb is masculine, because it is watching the subject.

common_error.why_en: Neither भूलना nor जाना takes ने, so there are two reasons the subject stays plain.

practice.prompt_en: He clean forgot the name. Pick the vector.
practice.question: वह नाम भूल ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: भूल जाना is the standard compound, and जाना brings no ने.

game.question_en: You want to say you simply forgot — the everyday way to put it.
game.explanation_en: All four are grammatical. भूल गया is what people say; भूला is correct but literary; the others are habitual and progressive.

items.pronunciation_notes: cha-laa jaa-naa. The first element is चला, not चल — and that is the point of this item.
items.gloss_en: to leave, to be gone — the one compound where both words move

learn.title_en: The exception to "only the vector inflects"
learn.explanation_en: चला जाना means to go away, to leave for good — and it breaks the rule this module has been building. वह चला गया, वह चली गई, वे चले गए: both words agree, not just the vector. This is a small closed set of idioms and चला जाना is by far the commonest member, so learn it as a unit rather than trying to derive it. Everything else about it is regular — चलना and जाना are both intransitive, so no ने, and the agreement is with the subject. Worth knowing that वह चल गई is not an error but a different sentence: it is what you say of a car that has started moving.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both correct but not the same. वह गया says he went; वह चला गया says he left, and the leaving is the point.

examples.note: Both words masculine singular.
Both words feminine. This is the irregularity.
Both plural. The pattern holds all the way through.

common_error.why_en: For "she left", the first element agrees too, giving चली. वह चल गई exists but means something else — it is what you say of a car that has started moving.

practice.prompt_en: She has left. Complete the first element.
practice.question: वह ___ गई।
practice.explanation_en: In चला जाना the first element agrees as well, so a feminine subject gives चली गई.

game.explanation_en: All four are grammatical. चली गई is departure; वह गई just says she went; वह चल गई is about something starting to move; the last is in progress.

summary.recap_en: ने appears only when the main verb and the vector are both transitive, so वह सब खा गया takes none even though खाना is transitive. भूल जाना is doubly exempt. And चला जाना is the one compound where the first element agrees too — चला गया, चली गई, चले गए.
summary.next_up_en: Next: पड़ना, for the things that happen to you before you can stop them.

items.pronunciation_notes: पड़ uses the flapped ṛ — the tongue flicks down off the roof of the mouth.

learn.title_en: पड़ना is what happens to you, suddenly
learn.explanation_en: पड़ना as a vector marks an action that is sudden, involuntary, and often unwanted. वह रो पड़ा is "he burst into tears" — not a decision, a collapse. Compare वह रोया, "he cried", which says nothing about how it began. पड़ना is intransitive, so there is no ने and the verb agrees with the subject. Of the four vectors this is the narrowest in meaning and therefore the easiest to place: if the action took the person by surprise, पड़ना is the one.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both correct. पड़ा says it came over him; रोया reports that he cried and leaves the manner open.

examples.note: Sudden and involuntary.
Neutral. Nothing about how it started.
अचानक and पड़ना reinforce each other.

common_error.why_en: रोना and पड़ना are both intransitive, so no ने.

practice.prompt_en: It came over him suddenly. Pick the vector.
practice.question: वह अचानक रो ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: पड़ना is the vector for something that takes the person by surprise.

game.question_en: He burst into tears — it came over him before he could stop it.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. रो पड़ा carries the suddenness; रोया simply reports the crying.

items.pronunciation_notes: हँस carries a nasal hum on the vowel: haṁs, one syllable.

learn.explanation_en: वह हँस पड़ी — she burst out laughing. Same involuntariness, and because the subject is feminine the vector is पड़ी. Worth noticing exactly what is agreeing here: there is no ने in the sentence, so the verb watches the subject, precisely as it did before Module 9 ever came up. The four forms are पड़ा, पड़ी, पड़े, पड़ीं, and which one you use depends only on who the subject is.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both correct. पड़ी says the laughter escaped her; हँसी just says she laughed.

examples.note: Feminine subject, so पड़ी.
Plural, so पड़े.
Neutral, and still perfectly good Hindi.

common_error.why_en: With a feminine subject and no ने in the sentence, the verb has to be feminine.

practice.prompt_en: The subject is feminine and singular. Complete the compound.
practice.question: वह हँस ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: No ने, so the verb agrees with the feminine singular subject: पड़ी.

game.question_en: She burst out laughing — she couldn't help it.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. हँस पड़ी is the one that says the laughter escaped her.

items.pronunciation_notes: Both consonants are retroflex and the ठ is aspirated: uṭh.

learn.explanation_en: उठ पड़ना is to get up abruptly, to spring up: वह उठ पड़ा. The involuntariness here is less about emotion and more about speed — no pause, no visible decision. Set it against वह उठा, which simply says he got up, and वह उठ गया, where जाना puts the emphasis on his now being up. Three vectors, three different things to say about the same movement, and none of the three is more correct than the others.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both correct. पड़ा makes it abrupt; उठा simply reports that he got up.

examples.note: Abrupt, no pause.
Neutral.
जाना, so the emphasis is that he is now up rather than on how fast it was.

common_error.why_en: उठना and पड़ना are both intransitive, so no ने.

practice.prompt_en: He sprang up, with no pause. Pick the vector.
practice.question: वह अचानक उठ ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: पड़ना for the abruptness. गया would say only that he ended up standing.

game.question_en: He sprang up — no pause, no visible decision.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct Hindi. उठ पड़ा carries the abruptness; उठ गया says he is now up; उठा simply reports it.

summary.recap_en: पड़ना marks the sudden and the involuntary — रो पड़ा, हँस पड़ी, उठ पड़ा. It is intransitive, so no ने, and the verb agrees with the subject. It is the narrowest of the four vectors and the easiest to place: if it took the person by surprise, use पड़ना.
summary.next_up_en: Next: पड़ना with a transitive main verb, and all four vectors side by side.

levels.title_en: The rule, and all four vectors

items.gloss_en: to blurt out — the second diagnostic

learn.title_en: A transitive main verb, and still no ने
learn.explanation_en: कहना is transitive — Module 9 made a point of it, setting उसने कहा against वह बोला. Put पड़ना behind it and the ने disappears: वह कह पड़ा. It is the same reason as खा गया. A compound takes ने only if both halves are transitive, and पड़ना is not. This is the second time the pattern has appeared, and once it clicks it covers every compound you will ever meet: look at the vector first, and if it is जाना or पड़ना, stop looking for ने.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both correct, and notice the subject changes. The simple transitive takes ने; the पड़ना compound does not.

examples.note: कहना is transitive and there is still no ने.
The simple verb, and here ने is required.
Feminine subject, feminine verb.

common_error.why_en: पड़ना is intransitive, so the compound is too — whatever कहना does on its own.

practice.prompt_en: He blurted it out before he could stop himself. Pick the vector.
practice.question: वह कह ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: पड़ना for the involuntariness — and note the subject stays वह, not उसने.

game.question_en: He blurted it out before he could stop himself.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. कह पड़ा is the involuntary one; कह दिया would mean he said it deliberately and finally. Notice the subject marking follows the vector.

items.gloss_en: it happened to him, or he let it out

learn.explanation_en: वह रो पड़ा and वह रो दिया are both correct and differ in who is in charge. पड़ा says it happened to him. दिया says he let it out — a trace of volition, the tears released rather than escaping. And here is where the ने rule earns its keep: neither takes ने. रोना is intransitive, so no compound built on it takes ने, whatever the vector is. देना being transitive is not enough on its own — both halves have to be.

vectorless_equivalent.with_vector: वह रो पड़ा। / वह रो दिया।
vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Three correct sentences: it overcame him, he let it out, or simply that he cried.

examples.note: It happened to him.
A trace of volition — and still no ने, because रोना is intransitive.
Neutral, and the third option as always.

common_error.why_en: ने needs both halves transitive. रोना is not, so देना cannot bring ने in by itself.

practice.prompt_en: It came over him and he had no say in it. Pick the vector.
practice.question: वह रो ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: पड़ा for the involuntary version. दिया would put a trace of choice back in.

game.question_en: He let the tears come — there was a trace of choice in it.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. रो दिया carries the trace of volition; रो पड़ा is the involuntary one; and neither takes ने.

items.gloss_en: the four vectors side by side

learn.explanation_en: You now have all four. लेना completes the action and keeps the result with you: मैंने खाना खा लिया. देना completes it and sends the result outward, or makes it decisive: मैंने खाना बना दिया. जाना completes it and marks a boundary crossed: वह आ गया, वह सो गया. पड़ना marks the sudden and involuntary: वह रो पड़ा. Two questions settle everything else. First, which shade do you want — including none, which is always available. Second, are the main verb and the vector both transitive? If yes, the sentence takes ने. If either one is not, it does not, which means जाना and पड़ना compounds never take ने at all.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: The plain form has been correct throughout these nine levels and remains the right answer whenever you have no shade to add.

examples.note: Both halves transitive, so ने.
जाना is intransitive, so no ने.
Neither half transitive, so no ने.

common_error.why_en: जाना is intransitive, so the compound is too, and ने has nothing to attach to.

practice.prompt_en: The laughter escaped her before she could stop it. Pick the vector.
practice.question: वह अचानक हँस ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: पड़ना for the involuntary, and पड़ी because the subject is feminine and there is no ने.

game.question_en: The work got finished — the state changed, and you are not saying who did it or for whom.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct Hindi. हो गया reports the change of state without an agent; the last two name a doer and take ने because both halves are transitive.

summary.recap_en: A compound takes ने only when the main verb and the vector are both transitive. कह पड़ा and रो दिया both take none, for the same reason from opposite directions. And the four vectors divide cleanly: लेना inward, देना outward or decisive, जाना a boundary crossed, पड़ना sudden and involuntary.
summary.next_up_en: Next: सकना — built the same way, but changing what the sentence claims rather than how it feels.

learn.title_en: सकना attaches to a stem, never to an infinitive
learn.explanation_en: सकना means "can", and like a vector it attaches to a bare stem: मैं कर सकता हूँ. It is never used with an infinitive — मैं यह करना सकता हूँ is not Hindi — and it never stands on its own. सकना is intransitive, so it takes no ने in any tense, and the verb agrees with the subject throughout: मैं कर सकता हूँ, वह कर सकती है, हम कर सकते हैं. One honest note: सकना is not a vector in the nuance sense. It changes what the sentence claims rather than shading how it feels. It sits here because it is built the same way.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Unlike लेना and देना, dropping सकना changes the meaning rather than the emphasis — from "I can do this" to "I do this".

examples.note: Bare stem कर, then सकता agreeing with मैं.
Feminine subject, so सकती.
Plural, so सकते हैं.

common_error.why_en: सकना takes a bare stem, never an infinitive.

practice.prompt_en: Complete the form that सकना requires.
practice.question: मैं यह ___ सकता हूँ।
practice.explanation_en: The bare stem कर. An infinitive cannot stand in front of सकना.

game.question_en: You want to say you are able to do this.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct Hindi, but only सकता claims ability. The others say you do it, you get it done, or you will do it.

items.gloss_en: to be able to go — and asking permission

learn.explanation_en: सकना works the same way with intransitive verbs: मैं जा सकता हूँ. Its most useful everyday job is asking permission — क्या मैं जा सकता हूँ? is "may I go?", and it is what you say to leave a room politely. The negative is मैं नहीं जा सकता, with the auxiliary usually dropped. And सकना never takes ने even in the perfective: मैं नहीं जा सका, not मैंने.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Again a change of meaning rather than shade — "I can go" against "I go".

examples.note: Bare stem जा.
The everyday permission question.
Negative, with the auxiliary dropped as usual.

common_error.why_en: सकना never takes ने, in any tense.

practice.prompt_en: Complete the form that सकना requires.
practice.question: क्या मैं ___ सकता हूँ?

game.question_en: You want to ask politely whether you may leave.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct Hindi. Only the second asks; the others announce that you are going.

learn.title_en: सकना agrees with the subject, always
learn.explanation_en: वह हिंदी बोल सकती है. There is no ने anywhere in a सकना sentence, so the verb agrees with the subject — and it is सकती carrying that agreement, not बोल. Same division of labour as every compound in this module: the first element is fixed, the last one moves. Worth checking against your Module 9 instincts: हिंदी is feminine and has no effect here at all, because there is no ने to make the object matter.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: "She can speak Hindi" against "she speaks Hindi" — again a change of claim, not of shade.

examples.note: सकती agrees with वह, not with हिंदी.
Same sentence, masculine subject.

examples.hindi: मैं थोड़ी हिंदी बोल सकता हूँ।
examples.read_as: maiṁ thoṛii hindii bol saktaa huuṁ.
examples.english: I can speak a little Hindi.
examples.note: The sentence you will actually use.

common_error.why_en: The first element stays a bare stem; only सकना inflects.

practice.prompt_en: The subject is feminine and singular. Complete the form.
practice.question: वह हिंदी बोल ___ है।
practice.explanation_en: No ने, so the verb agrees with the feminine singular subject: सकती.

game.question_en: You want to say you can speak a little Hindi.
options: मैं थोड़ी हिंदी बोल लेता हूँ।
मैं थोड़ी हिंदी बोल सकता हूँ।
options_read_as: maiṁ thoṛii hindii bol letaa huuṁ.
maiṁ thoṛii hindii bol saktaa huuṁ.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct and natural. मुझे हिंदी आती है from Module 10 is the closest rival and is about a learned skill; सकना is about being able to.

tts_strings: मैं थोड़ी हिंदी बोल सकता हूँ।

summary.recap_en: सकना means can, attaches to a bare stem, never takes an infinitive, and never takes ने. It agrees with the subject throughout. Unlike the four vectors it changes what the sentence claims rather than how it feels, which is why dropping it changes the meaning.
summary.next_up_en: Next: सकना in the past, its negative, and how it differs from Module 10's आना.
